title: GPU-SEAL provider policy record
description: One reviewed provider, CHARTER.md §7.4. A provider with no complete record here cannot be probed: the controller raises ProviderNotReviewed and the Phase 0 CI job keeps the no-named-provider rule in force.

template.description: Present only on the format template. The loader skips any record carrying it, so a template left in place can never be mistaken for a reviewed provider.

status.description: Only `reviewed` records enter the runtime matrix. An unreviewed slot is skipped entirely rather than loaded with a cautious classification — an empty matrix refuses everything, which is the safe state.

provider_code.description: Pseudonymous. CHARTER.md §7.6 forbids real names until methodology is validated, controls exist, measurements are repeated, provider responses are considered, and ethical review has passed.

pilot_category.description: Which Phase 2 slot this fills (CHARTER.md §11): hyperscaler, specialist, marketplace, or eu-sovereign. At least one EU-sovereign provider is required.

policy_sources.description: Where the reviewer read the terms, with retrieval dates. A classification without a source is an opinion.

policy_version.description: Version or date stamp of the terms as read. CHARTER.md §7.4 requires this in study metadata, not just the classification.

reviewed_on.description: A record older than 365 days is refused as stale.

notes.description: What the terms actually say about benchmarking and security testing, in the reviewer's words. Quote the operative sentence.

allOf.description: A reviewed record must actually carry the review.
Written permission is not optional for the class that is named after it.
